rationale: Jesus names the people and the event: "The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah" (12:41, BSB). Jonah 3:4-10 is that event: Jonah proclaims, "the Ninevites believed God," and God sees "that they had turned from their evil ways" (3:5, 3:10, BSB). The type is explicit_reference, not quotation, because nothing from Jonah 3 is quoted and no formula is used; this follows conn-matt11-elijah-malachi4, where Jesus names a figure without quoting. The Greek shows one shared word and one difference. Matthew's noun for "preaching," kerygma, is the Septuagint's word in Jonah 3:2 (BSB "message"). But Matthew's verb "repented" (metenoesan) is not the Septuagint's verb for the Ninevites: Swete's text says they "believed" (enepisteusan) and "turned" (apestrepsan), and uses metanoeo only of God (3:9, 3:10). Luke 11:32 has the same saying. Graded explicit because the text names Nineveh, Jonah and his preaching.
